description: ESP32 Rust firmware starter using the esp-idf-svc + esp-idf-hal stack on top of the ESP-IDF (FreeRTOS). Includes WiFi scan, GPIO LED task, and a tiny HTTP server on :8080. For IoT firmware where you want Rust ergonomics on Espressif's Xtensa silicon without going fully no_std.

defaults.headline: Rust on ESP32, WiFi first-class
defaults.subheadline: esp-idf-svc + esp-idf-hal — FreeRTOS tasks, WiFi, GPIO and an HTTP server on port 8080.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick for ESP32 / ESP32-S3 / ESP32-C3 firmware in Rust when you want ESP-IDF services (WiFi, BT, NVS, partition table, HTTP server). For bare-metal Rust on ESP32 without FreeRTOS, use esp-hal no_std instead — that's a different family.
firstSteps: Install the esp-rs toolchain: cargo install espup && espup install
Source the exports: . $HOME/export-esp.sh (adds xtensa rustc + clang to PATH)
Install espflash: cargo install espflash cargo-espflash
Flash + monitor a connected board: cargo espflash flash --release --monitor
gotchas: xtensa-esp32-espidf requires the esp-rs forked rustc (installed by espup). Stock rustup nightly will NOT build this crate — rust-toolchain.toml must declare channel = "esp".
You MUST source $HOME/export-esp.sh in every shell before building. Without it, rustc cannot find the xtensa target and linking will fail with cryptic llvm errors.
esp-idf-sys builds the entire ESP-IDF C framework on first compile (~3-5 min). Cache .embuild/ between CI runs or every build is a cold build.
sdkconfig.defaults is the Kconfig seed. Editing it after first build requires deleting .embuild/ — runtime Kconfig is baked during the ESP-IDF cmake step, not re-read every cargo build.
FreeRTOS default task stack is 3584 bytes. WiFi + TLS + HTTP will blow it — bump CONFIG_ESP_MAIN_TASK_STACK_SIZE to 8192+ in sdkconfig.defaults (already set in this starter).
Logging with log::info! requires esp_idf_svc::log::EspLogger::initialize_default() early in main, before any println!. Raw println! over UART works but bypasses the ESP-IDF log level filters.
Cargo.toml must include [package.metadata.esp-idf-sys] with esp_idf_version — otherwise esp-idf-sys pins to an old IDF and WiFi APIs shift under you.
